verdict.line: You win the poke-and-wave war before level 6, but a clean Rupture into Feast at any point afterward erases the lead and explains why this sits at just 46% over 274 games.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture) reaches 950 range against Parrrley's 625, so he decides when the poke war opens, not you. Gangplank's real edge is in the grindy in-between — stacked Grog-Soaked Blade poison and superior late scaling off Essence Reaver and The Collector eventually outpace Cho'Gath's flat tank stats — but every time you misjudge his Q cooldown or his level-6 Feast threat, he converts a bad step into a kill. The matchup is won on discipline around one cooldown, not raw stats.

theirWindow.when: Rupture is up and you're near 950 range
theirWindow.what: He can knock you up and slow you from outside your Parrrley range, then close with Vorpal Spikes autos or Feral Scream's silence. At level 6+ a slowed, low-health target also eats a 175-range Feast for true damage and an execute if it finishes you.

yourWindow.when: he just cast or whiffed Rupture
yourWindow.what: You have a hard 9-second window where his only ranged tool is down. Step up to melee-trade through the poison DoT and Vorpal Spikes exchange, or free-poke with Parrrley since he can't threaten the knockup-slow follow-up.

start.why: Sustains you through Vorpal Spikes chip damage during the early poke war, run in 72.4% of games at 44.5% win rate.

boots.why: The ability haste shortens Parrrley's 5s cooldown and Remove Scurvy's 22-18s cooldown, letting you contest the Rupture cooldown war more often — the higher-winning boots pick at 57.7% over 71 games.

core.why: Mana sustain plus AD lets you spam Parrrley to punish every missed Rupture without running dry.
Execute threshold turns poison ticks plus a Parrrley into a kill during his low-HP Feast windows.
Armor penetration cuts through Cho'Gath's stacking max-HP tankiness from Feast growth; this exact path wins at 54.8% over 42 games.

situational.when: the game runs long and you need bigger crit spikes over flat penetration
cho'gath or his jungler is threatening to all-in you off a landed rupture
you need a dash to punish him the instant rupture goes on cooldown
the lane turns into a sustained poke war and you need the lifesteal over haste

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacks a burn on top of Grog-Soaked Blade's poison every time you land an auto or Parrrley, which is exactly the kind of DoT pressure that wins the 3-5 and 11-15 trading windows.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is run in 88.6% of games at 45.2% win rate here. Ignite denies the health Cho'Gath would recover from Carnivore on a kill and converts your poison-stack trades into early kill pressure instead of him just healing it back.

playing.title: Bait the Rupture
playing.detail: Walk up for CS and retreat to force him to spend Q on minions. A whiffed or wasted Rupture opens your 9-second trading window.

playing.title: Never extend into a live Rupture
playing.detail: If his Q is up and you're inside 950 range, you're one knockup-slow away from eating Vorpal Spikes autos or a Feral Scream silence on top.

playing.title: Stack poison before you commit
playing.detail: Land an auto or Parrrley first so Grog-Soaked Blade is already ticking — the damage keeps working even if you have to disengage mid-trade.

playing.title: Know the silence locks your cleanse
playing.detail: Feral Scream's silence stops you from casting Remove Scurvy, so if he lands it first he can follow with Rupture and you have no answer to the knockup-slow.

playing.title: Hold Remove Scurvy for the knockup, not the poke
playing.detail: Don't burn your 22-18s cooldown clearing chip damage — save it specifically to cleanse the Rupture slow before he closes with Feast at level 6+.

playing.title: Pop Raise Morale before all-ins
playing.detail: The AD and movement speed buff wins straight melee exchanges once you're past level 5 and committed to trading through Vorpal Spikes.

playing.title: Use Cannon Barrage off-lane when the wave stalls
playing.detail: This matchup plays defensively; if the lane goes passive, your global-range ultimate lets you contribute to other lanes instead of forcing a bad fight into a stacked Feast.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and all win rates above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the cooldown reasoning, trade windows, and sequencing calls are my own read on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Cho’Gath’s (Q) as it has a short cooldown. Keep this in mind while contesting lane often to gain control.
